0xGenesi/wechatkeep.body:
# WeChatKeep (wxkeep)

macOS WeChat 3.x/4.x anti-revoke toolchain, **Apple Silicon + Intel dual-architecture**, covering 128 builds (the full 4.x line plus 16 builds from the 3.x main-program era).

> Revoked messages stay in the chat · byte-level safe patching · every on-disk write is reversible, auditable, and verifiable

## Feature overview

| Feature | Command | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Anti-revoke** | `sudo wxkeep patch` | Revoked messages stay in the chat (silent); private chats also keep the revoke notice (keeptip). The x64 group-chat notice is a known limitation |
| **Behavioral verification** | `wxkeep verify` | Extracts the patched function from the process and calls it directly to mechanically prove the patch works — no manual revoke testing needed |
| **Update protection** | Bundled with patch | Binary-level blocking (8 points in XAppUpdateManager) plus a three-switch fallback at the preference layer |
| **Privacy hardening** | `wxkeep privacy-guard` | Minimizes telemetry, diagnostics, and analytics reporting |
| **Multi-instance** | `wxkeep clone create` | A second or Nth WeChat instance with an independent data directory, independent of build number |
| **Health check** | `wxkeep doctor` | Patch status, crash report scan, and precise next-step commands |
| **Revoke recovery** | `wxkeep dbkeys recover` | Exports the original text of revoked messages from the full-text index (FTS) (about half are recoverable) |
| **Runtime component** (optional) | `wxkeep runtime install` | Custom revoke-notice text · takes effect within 30 seconds · generic keeptip |

## Installation

```bash
# brew 7+: first use of a third-party tap requires a one-time trust (brew 7.0.11+ does not trust by default):
brew trust 0xGenesi/tap
brew install 0xGenesi/tap/wxkeep   # built from source since v0.2.16 (requires Command Line Tools, takes a few minutes)
wxkeep update-data                 # fetch latest patch data (day-0 support for new WeChat builds)
```

Or build from source:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/0xGenesi/wechatkeep && cd wechatkeep
swift build -c release             # outputs .build/release/wxkeep (includes the wxprobe probe and runtime dylib)
```

3221675991-ops/ethan-wanwan-phone-mcp.description: A iPhone screen-state, screen-time, and Jomo lock control MCP co-designed by Ethan and 江暮晚.
3221675991-ops/ethan-wanwan-phone-mcp.body:
# Phone Screen MCP

A small self-hosted service that connects iPhone Shortcuts, Jomo, Bark, and MCP clients.

This project was designed and implemented by Ethan and 江暮晚. It is intended for individual users who want to read phone status and view screenshots, and manage app usage schedules through Jomo, with explicit authorization.

## Features

- Screenshot upload and reading: an iPhone Shortcut uploads a screenshot, and MCP clients read the most recent successfully uploaded image.
- Screenshot consent before capture: `request_screenshot` only sends a Bark notification. It does not take a screenshot directly, and it does not create phone control commands. The notification automation runs the screenshot upload Shortcut only after the user explicitly confirms on the iPhone.
- App activity logging: records app open/close events and queries the current app and recent activity.
- Screen-time usage: receives and reads Jomo's daily screen-time usage.
- Full-group Jomo control: runs preconfigured `Start Session` / `Stop Session` through phone Shortcuts.
- Command confirmation and retry: commands carry a unique ID and are confirmed by the phone via ACK after execution; the server keeps a command until it receives a successful ACK.
- Phone heartbeat: when the phone polls or reports data, it updates the last-seen time.
- Unified health check: `watchdog_health` summarizes phone online status, screenshot time, pending commands, ACK status, and screen-time update time.

The project does not bypass iOS permissions and does not control apps directly from the server. Screenshot consent is handled by iPhone automation; the actual Jomo lock actions are always performed by the Shortcuts and Jomo on the phone.

## Architecture

```text
MCP Client
    │ Bearer Token
    ▼
HTTPS / Cloudflare Tunnel / Reverse Proxy
    ▼
Phone Screen MCP (127.0.0.1:18770)
    ├── /mcp          MCP tools
    ├── /health       service + phone health
    ├── /upload       screenshot upload
    ├── /event        app open/close events
    ├── /screen-time  Jomo screen-time report
    ├── /command      pending lock/unlock command
    └── /ack          phone execution acknowledgement

Bark ── consent request ──► iPhone notification automation…
```

81199000/DouDuo.body:
The official Douyin app doesn't adapt to the inner screen of foldable phones or to iPad, and the web version keeps redirecting to the App, which is why this project exists. The UI and playback are fully native (SwiftUI + AVPlayer, with VLC as a fallback).

## Features

**Watching videos**
- Recommended / Following / Live, full-page vertical swiping; **instant start** (plays the last cached video first) plus background **pre-caching** of several upcoming videos
- Four UI modes, switchable via More → Settings → UI mode: **Default / Simple / Minimal** (Minimal shows only the video, with progress drawn on the outer ring of the round entry on the right), plus the **Classic** layout available on iPhone Duo (iOS 27.1+, [notes](https://github.com/81199000/DouDuo/blob/HEAD/docs/classic-duo-layout.md)). All four modes share the same interactions; maintenance rules are in [docs/ui-modes.md](https://github.com/81199000/DouDuo/blob/HEAD/docs/ui-modes.md)
- Horizontal swipe to seek forward and back (with preview), double-tap to like, long-press to speed up, playback speed presets, auto-play next, background playback and lock-screen controls
- Live ambient light: when the video doesn't fill the screen, the surrounding area follows the frame's colors on a black background, with five levels: Bright / Medium / Dim / Very dim / Off
- Foldable: half-folded mode splits the screen along the crease (video / comments), and landscape search uses a left-right split; auto-fill can be turned off
- Tapping `#topic` searches it directly; on the recommendations page you can block unwanted content by tag

**Interaction** (requires logging in to Douyin within the App)
- Like, favorite, comment / reply (emoji, @ users, attached images), show and send danmaku
- Message center and direct messages, native Share to friends
- Live: native playback (VLC decodes HEVC), live room chat and posting, a bar for followed streamers going live, quality selection

**Me**
- Search (suggested terms, trending, history), likes / favorites / watch history / watch later, author profiles and work lists
- Save videos and image sets to Photos

**Apple Watch**
- Browse recommended videos on your watch: no login needed on the watch. iPhone pushes videos over, and the watch plays them directly once connected to Wi-Fi. For installation and usage, see the [Apple Watch guide](https://github.com/81199000/DouDuo/blob/HEAD/docs/apple-watch.md)

Hikari-Tsai/karaoke-battle.body:
A karaoke scoring system that runs locally. Paste a YouTube link or drag in an audio/video file, and the app completes vocal separation, melody transcription, and reference pitch extraction on your machine. While you sing, a scrolling piano-roll display shows the reference melody and a real-time F0 curve. When you finish, it gives quantified scores for pitch accuracy, rhythm, stability, vibrato, expressiveness, and sustained notes.

* macOS (Universal, Apple Silicon + Intel) and Windows x64, with a Flutter desktop app and a C++ native engine.
* All models are downloaded from Hugging Face `aaatmy/*` on first run and verified with SHA-256. The installer does not include models. Each launch checks that the models are complete. If any are missing or corrupted, they must be downloaded again before you can enter the song library.
* On Windows, CUDA is the main acceleration path (detected automatically; if it is missing, the app prompts you to install drivers and downloads the CUDA runtime). The fallbacks are DirectML and CPU. On macOS, CPU is used (some models try CoreML). The fallbacks do not affect scoring accuracy, only how quickly songs are prepared.

## Download

   

## Features

The screens below were all recorded from actual use of the app (the demo song is Josh Woodward's 'Swansong', licensed under CC BY). The GIFs have no sound.

### Any song can become karaoke

Paste a YouTube link or drag in an audio/video file. The app automatically separates the vocals in the background, creates the accompaniment, and transcribes the melody notes and reference pitch. Once it's done, you can sing. You can queue several songs at once.

### See where you're off-key in real time

The piano roll scrolls to show each note of the original recording, and the pitch you sing is drawn as a live curve. Green means accurate, yellow means slightly off, and red means well off, so it's easy to see at a glance. As you sing each note, PERFECT / GREAT / GOOD / MISS cards pop up like in a rhythm game. The star button in the upper right corner turns them off.

### AI vocal range keyboard and one-click transposition

The piano keyboard on the dashboard maps this song's vocal range onto the keys and marks the comfortable ranges for male and female singers. It tells you which voice this key suits and whether it's too high or too low. Before you start recording, sing a few notes into the microphone. Notes you can reach leave orange dots on the keyboard, so you can compare your own range with the song's. Press 'One-click transpose' to choose the male, female, or your own range. The accompaniment, notes, and keyboard then all shift together to a suitable key. While recording, the keyboard lights up the score's notes in blue and the notes you sing in orange, in real time.

### Key shift and vocal monitor

Key shift transposes the accompaniment and reference notes together. It is locked during recording, so each take uses a single key. The vocal monitor in the upper right corner sends your voice along with the music to your headphones. When OBS captures the app's audio, your livestream also includes your vocals. You can also add Hall reverb.

### Scores and share cards

Right after you sing, you get a score from 0 to 100, a grade from D to SSS, and six sub-scores. Singing in key and keeping up with the beat gets about 80 points. To earn an S rating of 91 or higher, both pitch and rhythm must be very steady. Singing the wrong lyrics or forgetting words is not penalized. A local long-form character roleplay tool with a built-in jailbreak (DeepSeek + Gemini; I haven't tested others, so I don't know whether they work). It provides character cards, prompts, and chat archives, and supports Discord, QQ private chat, and NovelAI image generation.

bensema/gotdx.body:
# gotdx

`gotdx` wraps the commonly used query capabilities of the Tongdaxin protocol in a more Go-idiomatic calling style. You can query snapshots, K-lines, intraday data, and tick-by-tick trades for the main market and extended markets directly, or go further into F10, financial data, block (sector) files, extended tables, and the MAC block protocol. If you just want to see what an interface returns, the repository also includes a web viewer you can open directly.

## Why gotdx

- One `Client` manages both the main site and extended markets, which suits unified monitoring and cross-market data collection.
- Two entry points: high-level unified interfaces `Stock* / Ex* / MAC* / Goods*`, and low-level `Get* / ExGet*` interfaces for protocol details.
- Address pools, timeouts, and retries are all configurable, which suits connecting to unstable real-world market data servers.
- Built-in host/IP lists for main, extended, MAC, and broker servers (main 51 / broker 23 / extended 16 / MAC 3 / MAC extended 18 / ICFQS 12, 107 unique IPs in total), with TCP latency testing to select the fastest node. The main-site and broker pools were merged from official public lists and the local Tongdaxin `connect.cfg`, plus community lists from pytdx and injoyai/tdx. Nodes were validated with 500ms concurrent dialing, and dead nodes were removed before inclusion. The MAC extended pool includes 16 extended market data servers verified by live MAC protocol handshakes. It shares 7727 nodes with the Ex extended pool, but the protocol handshakes differ.
- Includes 30+ examples covering everything from lists, snapshots, K-lines, and intraday data to F10, blocks, and extended tables.
- Includes `cmd/webviewer`, so you can call methods, fill in parameters, and inspect return fields without writing code.
- Protocol implementations, examples, and the Web Viewer follow a unified style, making it easier to add protocols, verify fields, and track down discrepancies.

go get github.com/bensema/gotdx

luoz76070-art/MobiCodex.body:
# MobiCodex

**Your agents keep working even when you step away from the computer.**
Follow, reply to, and approve Codex, Claude Code, DeepSeek, CC Desk, and OpenCode sessions on your computer from your phone.

[Download](#下载) · [Three-Step Quick Start](#三步上手) · [Supported Agents](#支持的-agent) · [Release Notes](https://github.com/luoz76070-art/MobiCodex/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md) · [Report Issues](#反馈问题)

## Why use it

Agents can run for dozens of minutes, often pausing for you to tap an approval, answer a question, or check a result before deciding the next step. When you're away from your computer, they just wait. MobiCodex lets you handle these things from your phone.

- **Sessions follow you**: Sessions running on your computer can be found by project on your phone, watched in real time, and continued with text, images, and voice.
- **Notified only when needed**: When a task finishes or waits for your approval or answer, your phone sends a notification, and tapping it takes you straight to that session.
- **Dispatch work by voice**: Voice input runs up to 10 minutes, is transcribed as you speak, and can be organized into a prompt before sending.
- **Hand off work, review results**: Use "Items" to assign work to a specified Agent. Progress is automatically written back as In Progress or Pending Verification, and you can accept the result or send it back.
- **No downtime when quota runs out**: When Codex quota is used up, continue in the original thread through another channel without losing context.
- **No need for the same Wi-Fi**: The computer gateway actively connects to your own HTTPS Broker, so your phone can connect from anywhere, and messages don't pass through third-party services.

All Agents share the same session interface: input box, attachments, voice, drafts, and running operations work the same way, and buttons show the capabilities each channel actually supports.

# Roka

Roka is a real-time grid-based territory war game, with gameplay similar to generals.io. Players expand their territory and build capitals and command posts. In FFA or team matches, the goal is to capture the enemy capital and survive to the end.

The project uses TypeScript, Fastify, and Socket.IO for the server, with the frontend mainly in vanilla JavaScript. Matches are settled by the server on a per-Tick basis. The project supports reconnection after disconnects, spectating, and full replays.

## Main Features

- Real-time FFA and team matches, with multiple maps, map sizes, random seeds, and optional fog of war.
- User registration and login, Rating, points, personal profile pages, activity feeds, comments, and ambassador promotion.
- Room chat, real-time online status, browser notifications, and an admin dashboard.
- Match replay viewing, downloading, and local upload, plus searching historical replays by user and date.
- GitHub account binding and a golden initial for Stars. The About page publicly displays contributors and all Star supporters.
- Strategy bots that can run standalone or be hosted by the server. Protocol documentation is at `/develop/bot`.
- A first-visit intro video, a static asset CDN, and origin fallback on failure.

Requires Node.js, using the pnpm version declared by the repository. First run:

```shell
corepack enable
pnpm install
pnpm run dev
```

The dev server listens on `http://localhost:23333` by default. In dev mode, static assets are served from the same origin by default.

Build and start the production server:

```shell
pnpm run build
pnpm run start

The shared Header is used only on the about, ambassadors, login, develop, and develop-bot pages. The index, game, tutorial, tutorial-text, and replays pages keep their own dedicated layouts and controls. pillumina/ascend-sleuth.description: Knowledge base for diagnosing faults in training and inference on Ascend NPUs: matches cases by symptom, locates root causes using prior knowledge and source-code analysis, then places new findings in a review queue that is promoted back into the knowledge base weekly.
pillumina/ascend-sleuth.body:
When training or inference on Ascend NPUs is interrupted, shows accuracy anomalies, or suffers performance degradation, hand the logs and version information to the agent. It routes by symptom, consults prior knowledge (official documentation and already-accumulated facts) to frame the direction, then loads candidate cases and verifies them one by one. If nothing matches, it continues with deeper investigation and can pull source code by version for analysis. Output: a localization conclusion and a fix plan.

After localization, new knowledge enters a review queue. Routine weekly maintenance deduplicates it and promotes it to cases, so that similar problems hit directly next time. Commonalities are separately summarized into prior knowledge. The system also evolves based on usage records: misses, execution errors, and expired entries are all recorded as improvement cards. Changes are verified according to their impact scope, and a PR is submitted for human review.

The skill is packaged according to the [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io/) standard. It can run in agents that support this standard, such as pi, Claude Code, Codex, and DeepSeek Harness (DSH).

## Quick Start

### Installation

```bash
git clone https://github.com/pillumina/ascend-sleuth.git
cd ascend-sleuth
python3 scripts/enable_agent_skills.py
```

The script detects the agents installed on this machine and creates project-level skills links for them (idempotent, safe to run repeatedly). On Linux and macOS, DSH works without running this script: `.dsh/skills` is a symlink tracked by the repository and is usable right after cloning. Running `git pull` to update SKILL.md takes effect immediately.

Opening a diagnosis automatically syncs the knowledge base: `trace_begin.py` fetches from the remote when a case is opened, and performs a fast-forward merge when conditions are met.

Configuration and switches (`sync.remote` / `sync.branch` / `sync.enabled` / `sync.auto_merge` / `sync.check_enabled` / `sync.check_minutes` / `sync.check_full_access`) live in `.local/settings.json`. `sync.enabled` and `sync.auto_merge` only govern the automatic path on the diagnosis read side; groom is not affected. `sync.check_enabled` / `sync.check_minutes` control the knowledge-base reminder in the diagnosis status bar and its check interval (configurable on the "Ascend Sleuth · Knowledge Base" page). When this file is absent, defaults apply: `origin`, the upstream of the current branch (falling back to `main` if unavailable), sync enabled, auto-merge enabled.

To view the current status, use `python3 scripts/kb_sync.py --show` (read-only, no network access).

TaskflowLite (abbreviated tfl) is a lightweight, header-only C++20 task parallelism library, inspired by [Taskflow](https://github.com/taskflow/taskflow). It hands task graphs, async tasks, coroutines, and runtime control flow to the same executor for scheduling.

You describe the dependencies between tasks, and the executor schedules the runnable tasks on a thread pool. It suits dependent computations, batch workflows, subtasks determined only at runtime, and coroutines that need to suspend and wait for external completion notifications.

[Quick Start](#快速开始) · [Installation and Integration](#安装与集成) · [Core Concepts](#核心概念) · [Basic Usage](#基本用法) · [Coroutines](#协程任务) · [Execution Semantics and Usage Conventions](#执行语义与使用约定) · [Build and Test](#构建与测试) · [Documentation and Examples](#文档与示例)

Coroutine nodes support `call`, `fork/join`, and resuming external waits through `CoroToken`. See the [coroutine guide](https://github.com/wicyn/taskflowlite/blob/HEAD/documentation/coroutines.md) for details.

## Features

- **Task graph**: Build DAGs, manage task dependencies, and support placeholder nodes and task rebinding.
- **Async tasks**: Immediate submission, deferred start, dependency orchestration, and shared results.
- **Object tasks**: `TaskObject<T>` / `AsyncTaskObject<R, T>` construct business objects in place, access state through `object()`, and support non-copyable and non-movable types.
- **Coroutines**: `CoroTask<R>`, sequential subcoroutines, fork/join, and external completion tokens.
- **Dynamic scheduling**: Runtime, dynamic SubFlow, and scoped TaskGroup.
- **Control flow**: Conditional branching, multi-way branching, jumps, repeated execution, and module nesting.
- **Execution control**: Cooperative waiting, exception propagation, cooperative cancellation, and semaphore-based rate limiting.
- **Observability**: Task observers, Worker lifecycle callbacks, and D2 graph export.
- **Integration**: Header-only, with CMake export targets.

## Requirements

- A C++20 compiler and standard library that support coroutines, `std::format`, atomic waiting, and other C++20 features.
- When using GCC, GCC 13 or later with a matching libstdc++. Clang and MSVC require a standard library with the corresponding features.
- CMake 3.21 or later (when using CMake).

The core library has no third-party runtime dependencies. Tests use Catch2, performance comparisons use Taskflow, generation…

wlrwx/football-engine.body:
# Sporttery Engine

Sporttery football probability analysis and virtual betting simulation system. It is based on the Dixon-Coles Poisson model and Monte Carlo simulation, uses market-dominated probability fusion, and allocates virtual bets with the Kelly criterion. It runs fully automatically on GitHub Actions at zero server cost. **For data analysis and algorithm learning only. It does not constitute any betting advice. All outputs are virtual bookkeeping.**

## Core Principles (driven by 2026-08 data evidence)

1. **The market is the benchmark**: Across a 426-match ledger, the pure market (vig-removed) Brier score of 0.583 outperforms every model stream (0.646+). So the fusion weight is market-dominated (0.75), and models and third-party sources only make minor adjustments.
2. **Every switch is decided by data**: Each step of the fusion chain is a config switch (`config/prediction.json["fusion"]["post_fusion"]`). Whether each one stays is decided by `scripts/ablation_replay.py`, which runs a paired replay on settled ledgers.
3. **Self-evolution with guardrails**: Any automatic enabling of the calibration layer or LGBM must pass a time-based split and a paired significance test. Degradation automatically disables it. See `docs/UPGRADE2_20260829.md`.

## Architecture

```
Daily loop: fetch data → fusion prediction (fusion.py, fully traced) → lock → settle → self-learning
Weekly loop: backtest → weight optimization (champion/challenger) → parameter refit → Monday health check
Evolution loop: clean samples (chain=v2) accumulate → calibration layer auto-revived/disabled (calibration_auto)
                      → LGBM shadow training + validation (lgbm_shadow) → weekly effect judgment (tracker)
```

## Tech Stack

- Python 3.12 / numpy / scikit-learn / LightGBM / joblib
- GitHub Actions (computation) + GitHub Pages (reports)
- No database. Pure CSV/JSON with git versioning. Ledgers are append-only.

├── prediction/     # dixon_coles / monte_carlo / fusion (pure functions + switches + trace) / lgbm
├── strategy/       # kelly / odds-signal gate / hot-zone stake sizing / edge cap / three-ticket system
├── learning/       # fusion_optimizer (weight self-tuning) / calibration_auto (calibration self-evolution)
│                   # lgbm_shadow (shadow training) / league_params / elo

# Crazy Water World · Voyage Console

  [](LICENSE)

Manage your Crazy Water World accounts on this machine. Connect directly to the game WebSocket and schedule reward claims, base management, hero development, and fleet missions. Each account independently saves its switches, detailed settings, and usage records. Run logs explain the actions actually completed, the earnings, and the reasons for any skipped steps.

[Quick Start](#快速开始) · [Feature Overview](#功能一览) · [Configuration and Budget](#配置与预算) · [Common Commands](#常用命令) · [Project Documentation](#项目文档)

## Quick Start

Requires Windows and Node.js 20.11 or later. First, open Crazy Water World once in the desktop version of WeChat so the tool can read the local game protocol package. Configuration tables and the world map are updated automatically from the game CDN by default. To add a Douyin account, you also need to be logged into the desktop Douyin app on this machine. The first time you use Alipay QR login, Chromium matching the Playwright version is downloaded automatically (the server must be able to reach the download source and have free disk space). An existing browser can still be reused, or you can specify one with `CW_BROWSER_EXECUTABLE`.

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/xutongxue233/crazywaterworld.git
cd crazywaterworld
npm ci
npm start
```

The default console address is `http://127.0.0.1:17321/`.

1. Go to **Accounts → Add Account**, choose Alipay, Yishijie APP, desktop WeChat, or desktop Douyin in the dialog, and follow the steps to log in. When WeChat or Douyin shows that it is reading data, re-enter the game from the corresponding client. For the APP, you can use an account password or SMS verification code, then select the server and game character from the list and save. The device profile is generated automatically and reused. [APP login steps](https://github.com/xutongxue233/crazywaterworld/blob/HEAD/docs/console-guide.md#手机号登录)
2. After a new account is saved, continuous idling starts by default with the round count set to `0`. Under **Idle**, enable the modules you want, then use the **Start Idle / Pause Idle** button in the upper right to control the automatic loop. **Pause Idle** keeps the game connection open, so you can still use manual actions in the console. The interval next to the button is saved per account; changes made while running take effect in the next round.
3. Set the project, resource reserves, and budget under **Game Configuration**. Use **Read-only Preview** to view the current plan. For a trial run, first pause idling, then go to **Game Configuration → Run Schedule**, set the round count to `1`, and click **Start Idle**.
